text:
maria: uploaded a perfetto trace from the canary run (s3://perfetto/traces/1765004321). Seeing a 99p end-to-end spike. client->gateway->runtime spans look weird, putting snippets below.
ton y: looking now — initial span looks fine, then long wait before runtime deq, suspect batching / requeue. can you paste the timeline snippet? :eyes:
maria: snippet from perfetto UI: 
```
client_send -> gateway_recv (2ms)
gateway_dispatch -> runtime_enqueue (120ms)
runtime_dequeue -> kernel_selection (85ms)
kernel_launch (cudaLaunchKernel) -> first_token (200ms)
```
kv cache miss counter increments in the runtime_enqueue window.
suresh: 120ms in gateway_dispatch -> runtime_enqueue is suspicious. our batch_timeout is 80ms in canary config, so why 120ms? backpressure?
maria: canary used batch_timeout=80ms but perfetto shows repeated enqueue/requeue events causing longer waits. also observed many KV cache misses in the same window.
elaine: driver serialization could be inflating the kernel_launch time. do we have an nsys capture? perf-bot, any nsys attached?
perf-bot: nsys capture stored at s3://redwood-perf/nsys/1765004321-capture.qdrep (collected with --trace=nvtx,cuda).
tony: i pulled the perfetto timeline — kernel_selection is frequently choosing generic_kernel_v2 (higher reg usage). when that happens, cuLaunch latency jumps. looks like model shard mismatch hitting a non-optimized kernel path.
suresh: also check KV cache hit-rate around the spike. if hit-rate drops we may be doing full KV loads per request which kills latency.
maria: confirmed: kv_cache.hit_rate drops from 0.92 -> 0.12 during the 15:12:31-15:12:39 window. correlates with a model-version roll that landed on a subset of gateways. cold KV warmup + fallback kernel selection explain most of the spike.
elaine: notes / proposed actions: 
  1) tighten gateway->runtime model pinning during rollouts (avoid mixed versions),
  2) reduce batch_timeout to 30ms on hot routes to avoid long waits while warmup completes,
  3) update kernel selection policy to prefer low-register kernels during KV-cold windows,
  4) add NVTX spans around cuLaunch + kernel-selection decision so perfetto/nsys trace lines up exactly with drivers.
who wants which?
tony: i'll own kernel-selection policy change and a quick microbenchmark to validate lower reg kernels for perf.
suresh: i'll own the gateway pinning change + rollout checklist update. i'll also add a short alert when kv_hit_rate < 0.5 for 30s.
maria: i'll instrument NVTX around cuLaunch and re-run perfetto + nsys with identical load profile later today, upload traces to the same s3 path. i'll also temporarily lower batch_timeout on the canary.
elaine: i'll add a short doc blurb about kv-warmup behavior for platform teams and file an ops runbook note.
ton y: one more thing — the perfetto timeline shows repeated small requeues right before kernel_selection, like we're waiting for a batch slot and then re-enqueueing due to GPU overload. we should consider a soft-backoff in the batching heuristic to avoid thrashing. i'll prototype.
maria: thanks all, looping in @ops for rollout coordination. will post updated trace once done. :rocket:
